claude.country: USA, Sweden, Germany, Finland (TEDDY); USA, Canada, Australia (TrialNet)
models_evaluated: Original linear Cox landmark model (GRS2, autoantibodies, family history, age)

links.outcome: Calibration (Brier score) of TEDDY-derived model in TrialNet before vs after local recalibration
links.effect: Stratified model underestimated risk in TrialNet (Brier 0.40); logistic recalibration improved Brier to 0.16 (p<0.001); ages 8-17: 0.403 to 0.161.
links.quote: We observed significantly reduced Brier score values indiciating improved calibration in the recalibrated model compared to either the stratified or original prediction models (Fig. 3 ).

links.outcome: Effect of logistic recalibration on calibration in new cohort
links.effect: Logistic recalibration removed risk underestimation (about five-fold in children) and reduced Brier score from 0.40 to 0.16 in TrialNet.
links.quote: We observed that logisitic recalibration significantly improved the model’s performance, removing the underestimation of risk and resulting in more accurate and calibrated predictions (Fig. 2 , Additional File 3—Table S2C).

links.outcome: Differences between development and validation cohorts' baseline risk affecting model calibration
links.effect: 5-year T1D risk TrialNet 35% vs TEDDY 2% (p<0.001); model underestimated risk about five-fold in children under 8 (predicted 10% vs observed 50%).
links.quote: With an observed probability of 50%, predicted risk estimates are underestimated by approximately five-fold in children under 8 years old (predicted risk: 10%) and in those aged 8–17 years (predicted risk: 9%), while understimation was approximately 2.5-fold in adults (predicted risk: 20%).

links.outcome: Model calibration when applied to new screening population beyond development context
links.effect: Model discriminated comparably (3-year AUC 0.712 TrialNet vs 0.756 TEDDY) but was poorly calibrated in TrialNet (Brier 0.40) until recalibrated.
links.quote: As expected, given differences in cohort selection criteria, we observed consistent underestimation of the risk of type 1 diabetes in TrialNet (Additional File 2—Figure S5).

links.outcome: Performance of model in external validation cohort vs internal development cohort
links.effect: External validation in TrialNet showed similar discrimination but inferior calibration (Brier 0.40) versus development cohort.
links.quote: The stratified model showed similar discriminative ability in autoantibody-positive participants across TEDDY and TrialNet, but inferior calibration in TrialNet (Brier score 0.40 [95% CI 0.38,0.43]).

unlisted_practices: Logistic recalibration of survival prediction model to new screening cohort baseline risk
Stratifying prediction model by autoantibody status to address heterogeneity
Providing web-based individual risk calculator with visualisations

openai.country: USA, Sweden, Germany, Finland, Canada, Australia

links.effect: External TrialNet calibration was inferior: Brier score 0.40 [95% CI 0.38,0.43].
links.quote: The stratified model showed similar discriminative ability in autoantibody-positive participants across TEDDY and TrialNet, but inferior calibration in TrialNet (Brier score 0.40 [95% CI 0.38,0.43]).

links.effect: At 50% observed probability, predicted risk was 10% (<8 years), 9% (8–17), and 20% (adults).
links.quote: With an observed probability of 50%, predicted risk estimates are underestimated by approximately five-fold in children under 8 years old (predicted risk: 10%) and in those aged 8–17 years (predicted risk: 9%), while understimation was approximately 2.5-fold in adults (predicted risk: 20%).

links.effect: Ages 8–17 Brier improved from 0.403 [95% CI 0.375,0.430] to 0.161 [95% CI 0.144,0.166]; difference=0.2422.
links.quote: The difference between the Brier Score in the recalibrated model compared to the stratified prediction model was largest in participants aged between 8 and 17 years old (stratified model Brier Score = 0.403 [95% CI 0.375,0.430]; recalibrated model Brier Score = 0.161 [95% CI 0.144,0.166]; difference = 0.2422).

links.effect: The TEDDY-derived model underestimated TrialNet risk; 50% observed risk was predicted as 10%, 9%, and 20% across age groups.
links.quote: With an observed probability of 50%, predicted risk estimates are underestimated by approximately five-fold in children under 8 years old (predicted risk: 10%) and in those aged 8–17 years (predicted risk: 9%), while understimation was approximately 2.5-fold in adults (predicted risk: 20%).

links.outcome: calibration Brier score after logistic recalibration
links.effect: Brier score improved from 0.403 (95% CI 0.375, 0.430) to 0.161 (95% CI 0.144, 0.166) in participants aged 8 to 17 years (difference 0.2422)
links.quote: The difference between the Brier Score in the recalibrated model compared to the stratified prediction model was largest in participants aged between 8 and 17 years old (stratified model Brier Score = 0.403 [95% CI 0.375,0.430]; recalibrated model Brier Score = 0.161 [95% CI 0.144,0.166]; difference = 0.2422).
